It felt he was busy, but often he was unproductive. The challenge at hand during those long days was to become re-inspired and re-motivated, and to rediscover the need to create, imagine and rethink. 

He compares a initial experience to being away on island for X weeks on end. Being stuck in one spot is deceiving and it may be harmless, but the mind can start to go backward until you find something to interest it again - to engage it again. May be don't think of it as BOREDOM, but inneficiency or perhaps depression. 

When you're feeling bored you can jokingly say "Today is a chill day, I don't feel like getting anything done. I feel like enjoying myself in a relaxing setting". Boredom is an invitation to do something different, and see if you can enjoy it. Try something new, perhaps, if you like it, or even just not hate it. 

It is tempting to find yourself on a problem by hitting a wall and discovering there is no traction in finding a solution, it happens to software engineers too - try something else try something new, and we look at different problems, or even that same problem, on different days with a different mind.

While it's true that you are also capable of resolving your part of the problem — after all, your husband isn't controlling the state of your mind — begin by working on your husband. If that fails, and it might, you will then have to choose between leaving the relationship or accept the situation for what it is. Leaving the relationship at this stage may seem like a chucking out of the baby with the bathwater, but if your situation permits it, you have three options.
